issuer: a licensing officer under the Traffic Act (Cap. 24.03)
note: Read 2026-11-03 on the Attorney General's Office's legislation site (ago.gov.to). The Traffic Act (Cap. 24.03), 2020 Revised Edition, s. 15: a licensing officer issues a motor driver's licence on payment of the prescribed fee, to no one under eighteen (s. 15(2)); a first licence, to someone who hasn't held one for at least a year, is in force one year (s. 15(3)(a)), later ones 1, 3, 5 or 10 years at the holder's option (s. 15(3)(b)). The first licence, one year, is the one held, as the Bahamas' is. The Traffic Regulations (Cap. 24.03.01, 2020 Revised Edition), Fourth Schedule: the application for a new licence is free; a private-vehicle licence costs T$60 for one year (the fee held), T$150 for three and T$240 for five; ten years isn't priced. The theory and practical tests (T$20 each) aren't held. Matangi Tonga reported the same T$60 (trade press, agreeing). No identity card and no exchange list were read.

sources.said: (2) A motor driver's licence shall not be issued to any person who is under the age of 18 years. (3) A motor driver’s licence shall remain in force as follows – (a) the first driver’s licence issued to a person in Tonga who has not previously held a valid driver’s licence for a period of at least one year, shall remain in force for one year; (b) subject to paragraph (a) a driver’s licence may be issued to a person and remain in force for periods of 1 year, 3 years, 5 years or 10 years at their option
